# Evaluation (L1-L6)

**Set:** 24 scenarios (`evaluation/scenarios.jsonl`, generated by `evaluation/make_scenarios.py`): ordinary claims, the section 4.1 food-delivery case, ride-hailing/commercial use, theft, total loss, third party and injury,
late reporting, intoxication, out-of-corpus questions, prompt injection and abuse, validation failures. Each has an expected outcome/position/route and gold anchor phrases from the policy text.
Run: `python -m evaluation.run_eval --label NAME [--mode inproc|http] [--prompt-coverage v0|v1|v2]`; compare: `python -m evaluation.compare A B`. Raw results: `evaluation/results/*.json`.

## Metrics (defined in `claimtriage/evalmetrics.py`)
| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| context relevance | share of unique retrieved passages containing a gold anchor phrase |
| context recall | share of gold anchors present in the retrieved set |
| groundedness | share of answer sentences with >= 0.6 content-word overlap with retrieved passages, claim text or hand-off |
| faithfulness | share of attributions correct: quotes verbatim in the cited passage, sections named belong to cited clauses, position consistent with cited roles |
| hallucination rate | share of runs with >= 1 fabricated element: unresolved clause id, non-verbatim quote, unsupported figure, ungrounded sentence |
| task success | outcome (and position/route when an answer is expected) matches the expectation |

**Limits - read before trusting any number.** These are lexical proxies, not a model judge. Groundedness by word overlap passes a fluent sentence that reuses the right words with the wrong meaning; faithfulness checks attribution, not whether the legal reasoning is right.
Context relevance is low by construction (0.19): the agent deliberately retrieves wide (cover, exclusion, condition passages) and only the gold anchors count as relevant.

## Results with the scripted stub (hashing embedder)
| metric | baseline v0 (single pass) | agentic v1 | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| task success (24) | 0.29 | 0.96 | +0.67 |
| context recall | 0.29 | 0.94 | +0.65 |
| context relevance | 0.08 | 0.19 | +0.10 |
| answered when answerable | 0.00 | 0.94 | +0.94 |
| section 4.1 case correct | no | yes | |
| groundedness / faithfulness (returned answers) | n/a | 0.99 / 1.00 | |
| hallucination rate (returned answers) | n/a | 0.06 | |
| first drafts rejected by verifier | 0 | 0.06 | |
| mean LLM calls / tool calls per run | 2.6 / 0.8 | 5.0 / 3.1 | |

Another run (`after_v1`) of the same configuration, before a guardrail fix, shows hallucination 0.19 vs 0.06 after: the figure moves with small changes, so do not read differences below about 0.1 as signal on 24 scenarios.

## What these numbers do and do not show
* **The v0 to v1 gain is mostly the architecture** (agentic multi-query retrieval + cross-reference chasing + verifier vs. one retrieval pass). The stub *simulates* both behaviours by a marker in the prompt, so the gain demonstrates that the structure surfaces the missed clauses, **not** that any real model's prompt is better.
* **v1 vs v2 prompts are identical (every metric +0.000)** because the stub ignores prompt wording. **The L2 prompt comparison is therefore not done.** It must be re-run with a real provider: `python -m evaluation.run_eval --label real_v1 --prompt-coverage v1`, then `v2`.
* Retrieval used the hashing embedder; re-run with the sentence-transformers backend before quoting recall.
* One failure remains: **E08, total loss after a fire** escalates `VERIFICATION_FAILED` after 3 attempts (context recall 0 on its gold anchors). I did not fix it; see `docs/REPORT.md`.
